title: Platform operator — wire shapes, version 1
description: The machine-readable half of platform-operator-v1.contract.yaml. BOTH ARE NORMATIVE TOGETHER. Nothing in this repository executes JSON Schema: there is no implementation, no package.json and no node_modules, so this file is normative and hand-checked, never machine-validated. No report may describe it as validated.

organizationId.description: An opaque, non-sequential, unguessable identifier. 128 bits of base64url as generated (kernel/ids.ts), 22 characters; the bound is wider than the generator so a longer historical value is not rejected. It is NEVER parsed, decoded or interpreted by a client.

principalId.description: Same shape and same rules as organizationId. A separate definition rather than a $ref to it, deliberately: the two are different KINDS of identifier that happen to share a grammar, and one $def would let a future widening of one silently widen the other.

organizationStatus.description: As stored in the control plane's organization table. A closed set; an unrecognised stored value is never rendered to a client, because Core validates on read and treats an unknown value as unavailable rather than passing it through.

platformRole.description: The closed union stored in platform_operator.platform_role, mirroring permission-catalog.yaml's two platform-scope seed roles. An unrecognised stored value denies everything and never reaches a response.

permissionId.description: A registered permission identifier. The pattern is permission-catalog.yaml's namePattern, restated rather than $ref-ed because that file is YAML and this is JSON — a divergence between them is a defect qa-agent should catch, and the catalog is the authority.

cursor.description: An opaque, tenant-bound pagination cursor. Never constructed, parsed or modified by a client. Null means there is no further page.

organizationSummary.description: One row of the platform's Organization list. NOTE WHAT IS ABSENT AND WHY: there is no name, because control-plane/0002_organization.sql declined a name column and the organization-structure slice owns it; and there is NO COUNT OF ANYTHING — no customers, no members, no activity, no usage. Every one of those would be a read behind whereWithTenant, and a console acquires cross-tenant reach one convenient number at a time.

display_name.description: ALWAYS null today. Present in the shape so that adding names later is additive for both clients rather than a new field appearing in a published response. A client renders organization_id verbatim when this is null and must not substitute a placeholder of its own.

whoamiOutput.description: The calling operator's own context. IT HAS NO FIELD NAMING ANOTHER PRINCIPAL, and none may be added: the safety argument for this route is in its signature, not in a check.

permissions.description: The effective permission list, for rendering only. UI HIDING IS PRESENTATION, NEVER SECURITY (0007 D8): every permission here is enforced again by Core on the call itself, and a console that ignored this list entirely would be ugly and exactly as safe.
